name: Multi-Channel Processing Style Modulation — How Environmental Features Shift Cognition Between Divergent and Convergent Modes
short_description: Three pathways modulate processing style: (A) Disfluency from noise/complexity triggers abstract construal; (B) Spaciousness expands prediction envelope; (C) Comfort frees executive resources for internal search
structural_pattern: Environmental features modulate creative processing through THREE converging pathways: PATHWAY A (DISFLUENCY): Moderate ambient noise (~70 dB), visual clutter, or mild processing difficulty triggers a shift to abstract, higher-level construal — the brain 'zooms out' when it cannot process fine-grained detail, facilitating divergent associations. PATHWAY B (SPACIOUSNESS): High ceilings (R_h 0.35–0.50), open spaces, and dim lighting (~150 lux) expand the psychological prediction envelope, inviting abstract, relational processing rather than concrete, item-specific processing. PATHWAY C (RESOURCE REALLOCATION): Thermal comfort, natural materials (preattentive processing), and reduced external salience free executive resources from environmental monitoring, making them available for internally directed creative search. These three pathways converge on abstract processing that supports divergent thinking. CRITICAL TRADEOFF: Features that promote divergent thinking impair convergent thinking.
higher_order_principle: Environmental features modulate the position of cognition in a deliberate-constraint × automatic-constraint space (Christoff). The creative sweet spot — moderate deliberate, low-to-moderate automatic — is achieved by environments that relax external executive demands while providing enough sensory content to fuel associative processes without capturing attention fully.

pathway_a_disfluency.mechanism: Processing disfluency → construal level shift → abstract processing → divergent thinking
pathway_a_disfluency.key_evidence: Mehta et al. (2012): ~70 dB ambient noise enhances divergent thinking (d ≈ 0.4-0.6) through abstract construal shift
boundary_conditions: Speech noise with intelligible content is MORE disruptive
High noise (>85 dB) impairs both divergent and convergent

pathway_b_spaciousness.mechanism: Environmental spaciousness → expanded prediction envelope → abstract processing mode → divergent thinking
pathway_b_spaciousness.key_evidence: Meyers-Levy & Zhu (2007): high ceilings activate relational processing (~1,200 citations); Steidle & Werth (2013): dim lighting (~150 lux) promotes creativity through perceived freedom
boundary_conditions: Very high ceilings (R_h > 0.80) may trigger awe instead of creativity
Dim lighting impairs tasks requiring high-resolution visual processing

pathway_c_resource_reallocation.mechanism: Reduced external demand → executive resources freed from monitoring → redirected to internal creative search
pathway_c_resource_reallocation.key_evidence: Benedek & Fink (2019): creativity involves redirection of executive resources inward, not reduction. Environments that reduce external monitoring demand free resources for internal search.
boundary_conditions: Zero stimulation (sensory deprivation) provides no associative fuel
Pathway C alone is insufficient — must combine with Pathway A or B for creative benefit

spaciousness_calibration.note: VF3 'liberating' zone optimal for divergent thinking

pathway_independence_meta.hypothesis: Pathways are partially independent and produce additive effects
pathway_independence_meta.predicted_pattern: No significant three-way interaction if pathways independent; diminishing returns if shared bottleneck

divergent_convergent_tradeoff.description: Features promoting divergent thinking impair convergent thinking
divergent_convergent_tradeoff.evidence: Mehta et al. (2012): noise helped divergent, hurt convergent. Oppezzo & Schwartz (2014): walking helped divergent, trend toward impairing convergent.

causal_links.evidence_base: Mehta et al. (2012, ~1,100 citations): ~70 dB enhances divergent thinking vs. 50 dB or 85 dB.
Meyers-Levy & Zhu (2007, ~1,200 citations): high ceilings → relational processing; low ceilings → item-specific processing.
Steidle & Werth (2013, ~300 citations): dim lighting (~150 lux) enhances creativity mediated by perceived freedom.
Benedek & Fink (2019): creativity requires executive redirection, not reduction. Freed resources from external monitoring support internal creative search.

scope_conditions: Applies to individual creative work (not collaborative creativity)
Divergent thinking tasks (Alternative Uses, Remote Associates) are primary application
Convergent thinking tasks show OPPOSITE pattern — quiet, bright, enclosed is optimal
Multi-channel interaction (do pathways add or saturate?) not yet empirically resolved
moderators: Task type: divergent vs. convergent phases require opposite environments
Baseline creativity: low-creativity individuals benefit more from environmental support
Noise type: non-semantic (nature, coffee shop) superior to semantic (speech)
Duration of exposure: acute effects documented; chronic exposure effects unknown

interactions.nature: VF3 provides ceiling height parameterization (R_h). CREA2 adds creativity-specific prediction: R_h 0.35-0.50 optimal for divergent thinking.
L4's dim-warm ecological signal (evening → relaxation) feeds Pathways B and C. Dim light reduces external salience and signals low-threat context.
Natural materials engage preattentive multi-channel processing, reducing explicit monitoring demand (Pathway C).
CREA2 defines a creativity-specific Goldilocks, overlapping but distinct from T2. T2 predicts preference; CREA2 predicts creative output.
CREA2 specifies environmental inputs; CREA1 specifies the neural network dynamics these inputs modulate.
Reverse link added by CX V12 S3 remediation to satisfy bidirectional interaction encoding.
